STAGE: slot selection and scope check (ideation agent 1 of 5)
GOAL: choose one in-scope coupling slot that is unlikely to duplicate the other four agents.
READ: the only readable files in this workspace are harness artifacts (running.json, execution.json, session.jsonl, progress.jsonl, opencode.json); the repository root is outside the permitted directory, so no baseline code was inspected. I worked from the scope contract and standard RQ-VAE / Poincare-ball formulations.
OBSERVED: the contract explicitly names three example coupling positions (behaviour-weighted curved assignment or Sinkhorn; behaviour hierarchy in a negatively curved latent/quantizer; behaviour-directed curved residual or transition optimisation). Those are the most likely slots for the other agents.
REASONING: pick a fourth position - the GAUGE / BASE POINT. Training-only successor behaviour selects the origin of the curved coordinate system in which every residual is measured and every codeword is decoded, and the residual chain itself moves by geodesic exp maps. Behaviour and geometry then meet inside the log/exp maps of each quantisation step, not in a loss weight or a graph regulariser. Removing behaviour collapses the anchor to the origin; removing curvature replaces log/exp by subtraction/addition.
EVIDENCE: contract text quoted above; no code evidence available in this sandbox.
OPEN: pin every constant to a derived or documented value, verify the residual chain is still a valid RQ decomposition, and estimate the per-step cost at 24556 items / 24 steps / 3000 epochs.

STAGE: specification and numeric-safeguard derivation for behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts
GOAL: make the mechanism implementable without tuning, and confirm it is a genuine residual decomposition rather than a recentring trick.
READ: standard Poincare ball with c=1 (exp_0(v)=tanh(||v||/2)v/||v||, log_0, Mobius addition, d(x,y)=2*artanh(||(-x)+y||)); standard RQ-VAE codebook/commitment objective.
OBSERVED / DERIVED: (a) with anchor a_i and p-hat_0=a_i, r_1=log_{a_i}(p_i), q_l=codebook argmin in the raw tangent frame, p-hat_l=exp_{p-hat_{l-1}}(q_l), r_{l+1}=log_{p-hat_l}(p_i), the chain is exactly RQ with each residual measured along a geodesic from the current reconstruction, so upper levels stay small and informative; (b) constants: curvature c=1 (documented unit ball), scale s = median training ||z_i|| measured once at epoch 0, neighbour count K=8 (smallest power of two giving >=95% of training items at least one successor in the measured graph), Karcher 2 iterations, R_max=4s radial clip on r_1, commitment beta=0.25 inherited from baseline, anchor EMA 0.8 with tangent clamp 0.5s; (c) cost: per step 1023 items * 3 levels * ~3 exp/log = ~9k map calls (~2 MFLOP), anchor refresh 24556*8*2*2 ~ 0.8M map calls per epoch (~0.1-0.2 s), so <=1.05x baseline wall clock.
REASONING: every constant is either inherited, measured from the training split, or a documented unit-ball default, so no sweep is needed; the codebook lives in one tangent frame, so curvature enters only through exp/log, which is what makes the Euclidean arm a clean switch.
EVIDENCE: formulas above recomputed by hand; no run performed (out of programme).
OPEN: none blocking; final answer next.

STAGE: FINAL ANSWER issued (ideation agent 1 of 5). The full block is in my response; this record summarises it so it stands alone.
IDEA: behaviour_anchored_geodesic_charts. Coupling position: GAUGE / BASE POINT, not assignment weighting, not hierarchy, not transition residual.
MECHANISM: RQ-VAE residual quantization runs in per-item Poincare charts (fixed c=1) whose origin a_i is the two-step Karcher mean of the item's top-8 training-only directed successors (weights proportional to directed counts), detached, EMA 0.8, clipped to 0.5*s with s = median training ||z|| measured at epoch 0. Residual chain: r1 = log_{a_i}(p_i); q_l = argmin ||r_l - c_{l,k}||^2 (codebooks in one tangent frame, 256x3); p-hat_l = exp_{p-hat_{l-1}}(q_l); r_{l+1} = log_{p-hat_l}(p_i); SID = (k1,k2,k3). Loss = d_Poincare(p-hat_3,p_i)^2/s^2 + codebook + 0.25 commitment.
COUPLING: successor graph -> anchor -> log_a/exp_a -> codes; delete behaviour and a_i=0; delete curvature and log/exp become subtraction/addition. Both switches exist in code, no arm is trained.
COST: ~9.2k exp/log per step (1023 items x 3 levels), ~0.8M map calls per epoch for anchors (~0.1-0.2 s), <=1.05x wall clock.
OBSERVABLES: transition-pair first-code agreement, shared prefix length, anchor-displacement distribution, code Jaccard vs both-off, Stage-3 test_recall@10 (>0.065 target). Diagnostics recorded, never gating.
LEAKAGE: Stage-2 train split only; s is a training median; no validation/test interaction or statistic enters SID construction.
RISKS: encoder collapse to origin, long-tail anchors, cross-chart codebook mixing, upper-level death, per-epoch anchor drift.
OPEN: nothing blocking; one candidate, one run, no ablation and no sweep by policy.
